With FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS the online session is then deleted, so the encoded session type points at a session that no longer exists.

OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:110 creates the access token before generateRefreshToken() at :116, and the offline session is only created at TokenManager.java:1268. OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:117-120 then removes the online session when FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS is set. ClientCredentialsGrantType uses the same order. No decoder caller exists yet, so the impact is latent.

kept.claim: Only grants that go through createTokenResponse(), plus ROPC, refresh, standard token exchange and pre-authorized code, set Constants.GRANT_TYPE. Client credentials, UMA/permission (AuthorizationTokenService), legacy V1 token exchange and implicit/hybrid never set it, so their tokens are encoded with grant `na` even though `cc`, `pg` and `te` shortcuts are registered.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Grant type is not recorded for client_credentials, UMA, V1 token exchange and implicit flows

**Severity:** MEDIUM - several grants that have registered shortcuts will always encode `na`, so the new grant-type context is unreliable.

### The Problem
The grant type reaches the encoder only through `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)`. The PR sets it in:
- `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse()` (auth code, CIBA, device)
- `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`
- `TokenManager.refreshAccessToken`
- `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`
- `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType`

These token-issuing paths call `responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` directly and never set the attribute:
- `ClientCredentialsGrantType.java:140-141`: the client credentials grant. `ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns `"cc"` but it is never used.
- `AuthorizationTokenService.java:357-358`: the UMA ticket grant (`PermissionGrantTypeFactory`, shortcut `"pg"`).
- `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient` (line 409-410): legacy V1 token exchange, `"te"`.
- `OIDCLoginProtocol.java:272`: implicit/hybrid access tokens.

For these, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` falls back to `UNKNOWN = "na"`.

### Theory / Proof
The PR description says the grant type is needed for #37117 (token exchange). V1 token exchange tokens will still report `na`. Service-account tokens (client_credentials) are one of the most common machine-to-machine tokens, and they will never say `cc`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Encoding does not fail, because `na` is a valid shortcut. Any follow-up that relies on grant type (e.g. "was this token issued by client_credentials / token exchange?") will get `na` for these grants and silently take the wrong branch. The unit test `testSuccessClientCredentialsToken` builds `trltcc` by hand, so it hides the fact that the server never produces `cc`.

### Recommendation
Set the attribute on every grant path, preferably in one place. For example, in `TokenManager.AccessTokenResponseBuilder.generateAccessToken()` fall back to the grant from the request when the attribute is missing:
```java
// ClientCredentialsGrantType, before generateAccessToken()
clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType());
// AuthorizationTokenService
clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.UMA_GRANT_TYPE);
// AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient
clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);
```
Also add `AssertEvents` expectations for client credentials (`expectClientLogin`) that check the `cc` shortcut.
kept.evidence: GRANT_TYPE is set only at OAuth2GrantTypeBase:109, ROPC:134, TokenManager:248, StandardTokenExchangeProvider:237 and PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType:82. ClientCredentialsGrantType:140-141, AuthorizationTokenService:357-358, AbstractTokenExchangeProvider:409-410 and OIDCLoginProtocol:271-272 never set it, so those tokens get 'na'. Implicit/hybrid getting 'na' is arguably acceptable.

kept.claim: isAccessTokenId() reads the wrong substring (3,5 instead of 4,6) and returns false when the shortcut matches. The matcher therefore never checks the grant shortcut: it accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>`, and it would reject correct ids if the indices were fixed.
kept.evidence: AssertEvents.java:483 uses substring(3,5). The encoder/decoder layout puts the grant at substring(4,6) (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider:81). The first character of substring(3,5) is always 't' or 'n', so it never equals ac/dg/rt/ci and the inverted return false never runs. The matcher only checks for a UUID.

kept.claim: getShortcut() is added to the internal OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI with no default. Custom grant factories built against the old interface throw AbstractMethodError, and a null shortcut causes an NPE, in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, which aborts server startup. Since the SPI is internal this is allowed, but a default method or a migration note would avoid a confusing boot failure.
kept.evidence: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 is abstract, and postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-77, called from DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory:168) invokes it. AbstractMethodError or an NPE on a null shortcut aborts startup. However, OAuth2GrantTypeSpi.isInternal()=true and the interface lives in server-spi-private, where breaking changes are allowed by policy, so the severity was overstated.

kept.claim: The getShortcut() Javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but the decoder hard-requires a 6-char prefix with a 2-char grant shortcut, and postInit never validates length. A grant with a 3-char shortcut produces token ids that encode successfully but that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with IllegalArgumentException.
kept.evidence: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 Javadoc says 3 letters. The decoder requires a 6-char prefix with substring(4,6). encodeTokenId concatenates the shortcut without checking its length, and postInit only checks for duplicates.

kept.claim: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the grant shortcut belongs to a grant factory that is no longer registered (e.g. token-exchange, CIBA, device or OID4VC feature disabled after tokens were issued). Still-valid, signed tokens therefore become undecodable instead of degrading to UNKNOWN, as legacy UUID ids do.
kept.evidence: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:91-94 throws when the grant factory is absent. CIBA, device, token-exchange and pre-authorized-code are EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory implementations that drop out when their feature is disabled, while legacy ids degrade to UNKNOWN (:67-69). There is no production caller yet, so the impact is latent.

kept.claim: Copy-paste bug: the fourth null check tests grantType again (with message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'), so rawTokenId is never validated. A null raw id encodes to e.g. 'onrtac:null'.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `rawTokenId` null check actually re-checks `grantType`

**Severity:** LOW - the constructor's null-safety contract is not enforced for `rawTokenId`.

### The Problem
```java
Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");
Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
```
The second call checks `grantType` again, so `rawTokenId` is never checked.

### Theory / Proof
`new AccessTokenContext(ONLINE, REGULAR, "authorization_code", null)` succeeds. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` then produces `"onrtac" + ':' + null` = `onrtac:null`. That is a syntactically valid but non-unique `jti`, and RFC 7519 section 4.1.7 requires `jti` to be unique. A custom `TokenContextEncoderProvider` (the PR says the SPI exists to allow this) could hit it.

### Recommendation
```java
Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
```
kept.evidence: AccessTokenContext.java:73 checks grantType twice, so rawTokenId is never validated. encodeTokenId would produce 'onrtac:null'.
